summary:
Public Law 119-92, cited as the "Investing in All of America Act of 2025," amends the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 to modify the maximum leverage limits for Small Business Investment Companies (SBICs) and expand the categories of investments excluded from outstanding leverage calculations.

Section 2(a) amends Section 103(9) of the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 (15 U.S.C. 662(9)), which defines "private capital." The amendment removes the requirement that certain entities be established prior to October 1, 1987, and adds "foundation, endowment, or trust of any college or university" to the list of qualifying entities. It adds a new subparagraph (C) excluding funds obtained directly or indirectly from any Federal, State, or local government or instrumentality from the definition of private capital for the purpose of leverage approval, except for funds specifically described in the preceding subclauses.

Section 2(b) amends Section 303(b)(2) of the Act (15 U.S.C. 683(b)(2)) regarding maximum leverage. Subparagraph (A) is amended to reduce the general maximum leverage limit for a single company from $300,000,000 to $200,000,000. It establishes tiered limits: $250,000,000 for companies making quarterly or semiannual interest payments, and $175,000,000 for any other company licensed under section 301(c). Subparagraph (B) is similarly amended to set the maximum leverage for commonly controlled companies at $475,000,000 if they make quarterly or semiannual interest payments, and $350,000,000 for any other commonly controlled companies licensed under section 301(c).

Subparagraph (C) is amended to expand the leverage exclusion for investments in smaller enterprises. The exclusion now applies to investments in: (I) small business concerns located in low-income geographic areas (as defined in section 351 of the Act) or rural areas (as defined in section 343(a)(13) of the Agricultural Act of 1961); (II) small business concerns operating primarily in a covered technology category (as defined in 10 U.S.C. 149(e)); or (III) small manufacturers (as defined in section 501(e)(6) of the Act). The amendment imposes a limitation on this exclusion, capping the aggregate amount excluded at the lesser of 50 percent of the private capital of the company or companies or $125,000,000. Finally, the amendment includes a prospective applicability provision, stipulating that an investment is only eligible for the exclusion if made by the licensee after the date of enactment of the clause. The Act was approved on May 19, 2026.
